version.approval_notes: Source: attached. Build: Node.js 22+ (we use 26) and python3; in the source folder run `npm ci && npm run build`. The output in `dist/firefox` is the submitted add-on (not minified). The extension works only with a self-hosted paperus server (https://github.com/qcode-uni-a/paperus), which the user connects in the options page; it then gets an access token that may only add papers. Data goes only to that server, never to the developers. Since 0.0.11: (1) a content script registered at runtime (scripting.registerContentScripts) only for the connected paperus server's address marks its pages and relays requests from its Missing page; (2) on such a request the user may let the extension get PDFs of chosen papers: the optional host permission for websites is requested from an extension page on the user's click (allow.html), and each paper's publisher page is opened in a background tab to download its PDF with the user's own access, sent only to the user's paperus. (3) The right-click menu of the toolbar button saves to another owner (contextMenus). Since 0.0.17: (4) where a page cannot show why saving failed (Firefox's PDF viewer), a small extension window (note.html) does; if access to the PDF's site is missing, its button requests that optional host permission on the user's click and saves again. (5) The toolbar button's right-click menu also opens the options page. Since 0.0.18: (6) content_security_policy.extension_pages is "script-src 'self'", i.e. Firefox's default without upgrade-insecure-requests: self-hosted servers on a local network are often plain HTTP (e.g. a test server at http://<hostname>:8000), and the upgrade made every request to them fail. The options page warns the user in red when connecting to a plain-HTTP address other than localhost.
